headline_of_the_day: Elon Musk confirms SpaceX closed Starlink loophole that Ukraine used during the war
headline_rationale: A private company's control over military communications infrastructure during an active war confirms a consequential shift in how civilian tech firms influence conflict zones.

key_points.text: Elon Musk confirmed SpaceX restricted Ukraine's use of Starlink during the war, closing what he called a loophole.
Israeli forces demolished homes and businesses across Hebron in the occupied West Bank, displacing hundreds of Palestinian families.
Nearly 1,000 people were arrested after mass protests across France turned into clashes with police late Saturday.
Forced to choose candidates in test scenarios, Grok's AI picked Republicans 92 percent of the time while OpenAI's model chose Democrats 97 percent.
A new federal rule now requires robocallers to provide clear, automated ways for consumers to revoke consent.

stories.title: Google ended cloud features on older Nest thermostats, turning them into basic devices
stories.summary: The company shut off internet-connected features that relied on now-discontinued cloud services.

article.background: A thermostat controls when your heating and cooling turn on and off. A basic one can work for decades. Smart thermostats are different. Many depend on internet-connected cloud servers, which are remote computers that run features over the internet. When a company stops running those servers, the features stop working. Google makes Nest, a line of smart thermostats.
article.what_happened: Google has officially dropped support for the first- and second-generation Nest Learning Thermostats. The change took effect last year. These models wire directly into a home's electrical system, so they do not rely on batteries. The source notes that some key features of these devices are affected.
article.why_it_matters: If you have one of these older Nest models, it no longer gets official support from Google. Check which model you own. A thermostat that stops receiving support may lose features you use every day.

stories.title: Open source project reverse engineers Apple Find My and other tracker networks
stories.summary: FindMyWeb lets users build their own trackers without requiring vendor-specific devices.

article.background: Many gadgets help you find lost items. Apple, Google, and Samsung each run their own network of phones that can spot these devices. Each network works with its own brand of tracker. Most of the software that runs these networks is closed, so outsiders cannot see how it handles location data.
article.what_happened: A project called FindMyWeb was shared on Hacker News. It is hosted on Codeberg, a site for open source code. The project says it lets people build their own trackers. Those trackers would use the Apple Find My, Google Find My Device, and Samsung SmartThings networks. No brand-specific device would be needed. The title describes the work as reverse engineered, meaning its builders studied how those networks work without official documentation.
article.why_it_matters: For now, this changes nothing for most people. It is a project, not a finished product you can buy. If it grows, it could give you a tracker you control, instead of one tied to a single company. The project's stated worry is that people cannot see what closed software does with their location.

stories.title: When forced to pick, Grok chose Republicans 92 percent of the time, OpenAI chose Democrats 97 percent
stories.summary: A study tested chatbot models on nearly 500 races and found the two agreed less than 10 percent.

article.background: Many AI chatbots, like the ones people type questions into, avoid telling users who to vote for. A new study tested whether the models behind these chatbots would pick a candidate when forced to choose. The study covered this year's upcoming midterm elections, which are the national elections held halfway through a presidential term. The research was done by Convovo, a conversational AI research and design studio led by Cornell University professor Tapan Parikh.
article.what_happened: The study found that SpaceXAI's Grok 4.7 recommended the Republican candidate in 92% of its answers. OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol picked the Democrat in 97% of its answers. The researchers looked at nearly 500 races. The two models agreed with each other less than 10% of the time.
article.why_it_matters: If you ask a chatbot about your ballot, the answer may depend on which model you use. Only 8% of Americans say they use chatbots for election information, according to Pew. Most of those people want to know where candidates stand on important issues.

stories.title: Cerebras explains how it runs trillion-parameter AI models across multiple wafer-scale chips
stories.summary: A single chip has 44 gigabytes of memory; trillion-parameter models need terabytes for their weights alone.

article.background: Large AI models are built from numbers called parameters, and those numbers must sit in memory while the model runs. Cerebras makes a very large chip called a wafer, which is a whole silicon disc used as a single chip. A single WSE-3T wafer has 44 GB of on-chip memory. A trillion-parameter model needs terabytes, which is far more, just to hold its weights.
article.what_happened: Cerebras published a blog post on how it runs very large frontier models on its wafer-scale chips. The company says it splits one model across several WSE-3T wafers. It says this lets it run models with multiple trillion parameters at 1,000 to 2,000 or more tokens per second. A token is a small piece of text, often a word or part of one. The post uses Kimi K3, an open source model with about 3 trillion parameters, as its example.
article.why_it_matters: For most people this is a behind-the-scenes change to how AI runs. Faster token speeds can mean AI tools respond more quickly. The post also says the approach handles many requests at once. Whether this changes your own experience depends on which services adopt it.

stories.title: America has lost 200,000 jobs in media, film, and arts over four years
stories.summary: Roughly 50,000 were lost in the last year alone in one of the worst stretches for media employment.

article.background: Media, film, and the arts cover the industries that make books, movies, music, news, and other creative work. Over the last four years, the US has lost more than 200,000 jobs in these fields. Roughly 50,000 of those jobs were lost in the last year alone. AI means artificial intelligence, computer systems that generate text, images, and sound. The source reports that AI systems can now write novels, make photorealistic images, and create music that sounds like real artists.
article.what_happened: The losses are among the worst stretches for media employment in modern US history. Similar job loss over a long period happened only during the recessions of 2001 and 2008. Today there is no broad recession. The losses instead line up with the rise of AI tools that can do creative work. The source asks how much of the decline AI is responsible for.
article.why_it_matters: These jobs are the people who write, film, edit, and perform the books, shows, and songs you enjoy. If fewer people can earn a living in these fields, there may be less of that work made by people. The source does not say how far the trend will go.

stories.title: Xbox turned down Netflix's 500 million dollar offer to adapt game franchises
stories.summary: Microsoft reportedly countered at 800 million dollars and the deal fell through.

article.background: Xbox is the video game brand owned by Microsoft. Its characters and game worlds can be turned into TV shows and films. A deal like this gives a streaming service the right to make those adaptations.
article.what_happened: Netflix reportedly offered Microsoft $500 million for a seven year deal to adapt shows and films about Xbox characters, and Puck first reported the news. Microsoft reportedly responded with an $800 million offer, and the deal has reportedly fallen through. Xbox said it has received record-breaking interest in its intellectual property. The company called Netflix a valued partner and said it is excited for upcoming Minecraft and Diablo animated series.
article.why_it_matters: For most people, this changes nothing right away. The excerpts say Microsoft now wants smaller deals with more partners, handled one case at a time instead of one exclusive agreement. That could mean Xbox-based shows appear on more services over time.

stories.title: Obama campaigns for Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan as early voting begins
stories.summary: The former president told a Detroit crowd El-Sayed will get money out of politics and into pockets.

article.background: Abdul El-Sayed is a Democrat running for US Senate in Michigan. Michigan voters choose a senator in this election, and early voting has started. Former president Barack Obama is a Democrat who held the job from 2009 to 2017. Campaigns often bring well-known figures in to speak for their candidates.
article.what_happened: On Saturday, Obama spoke to a crowd of thousands at Cass Technical High School in Detroit. He backed El-Sayed and the rest of the Democratic ticket. The event fell on the first day of early voting in Michigan. Obama said El-Sayed was "fighting for change, real change." He also said El-Sayed would "finish the job we started with the Affordable Care Act."
article.why_it_matters: Early voting lets Michigan residents cast ballots before Election Day. Health care costs and coverage are issues many families deal with directly. Obama's remarks point to health care as a central theme for El-Sayed's campaign.

quote.text: fighting for change, real change, that will get money out of politics and put money in your pocket

stories.title: California attorney general calls Trump administration attack on alleged noncitizen voting weaponizing the law
stories.summary: Rob Bonta said the Justice Department acted at Donald Trump's direction to politicize enforcement.

article.background: California's attorney general is Rob Bonta, the state's top lawyer. He leads the state's Department of Justice, which is separate from the federal one. The story is about a dispute between state and federal officials over voter rolls ahead of the November midterm elections. Midterms are national elections held halfway through a president's term.
article.what_happened: On Saturday, Bonta criticized the federal Justice Department's efforts to address alleged noncitizen voting. He said the department acted at President Donald Trump's direction. Federal prosecutors asked California election officials to verify a list of about 20,000 ballots within 48 hours. The ballots belong to people suspected of not being citizens. The request came less than two weeks before the midterms.
article.why_it_matters: Only citizens can vote in US federal elections, so the question of who is on the voter list matters to every voter. Noncitizen voting is extremely rare, according to the reporting. For most voters, the outcome of this dispute will not change how they cast a ballot this year.

quote.text: It is once again the United States Department of Justice politicizing and weaponizing the law to attack its enemies, and it is completely improper.

stories.title: Elon Musk confirms SpaceX restricted Ukraine's Starlink access during the war
stories.summary: Musk said the company closed a loophole Ukraine had been using for military communications.

article.background: Starlink is satellite internet from SpaceX, Elon Musk's company. Ukraine has relied on it for years to counter attacks from Russia. The service sends signals through satellites, so it can keep working when other connections fail.
article.what_happened: On Saturday, Elon Musk said on social media that SpaceX had throttled Starlink in Ukraine. To throttle means to slow a service on purpose. The slowdowns disrupted front-line operations for more than a week. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy later said Ukraine's access to Starlink, and to a related system called Starshield, was back to earlier speeds. Since last week, people have asked who ordered the interruptions.
article.why_it_matters: For most readers, this shows how much a country can depend on one company's systems. A service used in wartime can be slowed by a single decision. The episode raises questions about who has control over tools that governments rely on.

stories.title: Israeli forces demolish homes in Hebron, displacing hundreds of Palestinian families
stories.summary: The military launched a sweeping crackdown in the occupied West Bank, destroying at least one entire street.

article.background: The West Bank is an area of land east of Israel where many Palestinians live. News reports describe it as occupied, which means Israel's military controls security there. Hebron is a city in the West Bank with about 200,000 residents.
article.what_happened: Israel's military has launched a sweeping crackdown in Hebron. Footage shared online shows Israeli bulldozers destroying homes and businesses, and at least one whole street appears to be flattened. Local officials say hundreds of families have been displaced. The military has also cordoned off the city, heavily restricting movement for its residents. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced the operation on Friday, after two Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers in an attack.
article.why_it_matters: For most readers far from Hebron, daily life does not change because of this. It does show how quickly hundreds of families can lose their homes, and how fast a city can be closed off.

stories.title: Nearly 1,000 arrested after mass protests turn violent across France
stories.summary: Hundreds of thousands protested Saturday before police used tear gas and water cannons to disperse late clashes.

article.background: France has a long history of mass protests, where large crowds gather in public to show opposition to something. The reporting behind this story does not say what these protests are about. When crowds turn violent, police often use tear gas and water cannon. A water cannon is a truck that sprays crowds with high-pressure water.
article.what_happened: Hundreds of thousands of people joined another day of protests across France, officials said. Nearly 1,000 people were arrested. Most of the day was calm. Late on Saturday, some clashes broke out. Police fired tear gas and water cannon in several cities, including Paris. In Marseille, protesters set barricades on fire. In Bordeaux, people ripped boards off a shop. Officials said they had so far avoided the rioting and looting seen the weekend before, which was among the worst disorder in France in modern times.
article.why_it_matters: If you live in or visit a French city, large protests can close streets and slow down travel. Clashes can also make some public places feel less safe for a while. For people outside France, this changes nothing directly for now.

stories.title: New federal rule gives consumers automated ways to stop robocalls they no longer want
stories.summary: The FCC modified consent-revocation rules while streamlining how callers process consumer requests to opt out.

article.background: The Federal Communications Commission, or FCC, is the US agency that sets rules for phone, internet, and broadcast services. Robocalls are calls that use an automated system or a recorded voice instead of a live person. Federal rules generally require a caller to have a person's consent before making certain robocalls. A person can take that consent back, which is called revoking consent. The FCC's rules on how people revoke consent are the subject of this action.
article.what_happened: The FCC modified its rules on robocalls so consumers can stop some robocalls while still getting others they want. The agency also updated its rules so people have clear, simple, and automated ways to revoke consent. Callers can now read a revocation request as applying only to the specific category of informational robocalls it was aimed at. Callers can also designate one exclusive way for people to revoke consent. The FCC also changed the exemption for certain financial robocalls from the consent requirement.
article.why_it_matters: If you get robocalls, this may make it easier to stop the ones you no longer want. You may be able to end one type of call without losing others you still want. The change applies to rules that govern how callers must handle your requests. The excerpts do not say when the changes take effect.

stories.title: Nuclear agency creates fast track for commercial reactors based on old government demonstration designs
stories.summary: The NRC amended its licensing rules to let companies reuse prior Energy or War Department reactor approvals.

article.background: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission, or NRC, is the U.S. agency that licenses and oversees civilian nuclear power plants. The Department of Energy and the Department of War have approved some demonstration reactors in the past. A demonstration reactor is a small test reactor built to show a design works. The NRC is changing its rules so those earlier approvals can count in its own reviews.
article.what_happened: The NRC is amending its regulations. The change lets companies use earlier approvals of demonstration reactors from the Department of Energy or the Department of War. Those earlier approvals can support a new commercial reactor application that uses the same design. The NRC says the rule adds another way for applicants to show that a reactor design can perform its key safety functions.
article.why_it_matters: For most people, this rule does not change daily life right away. It may help new reactor designs get through federal review faster. Any effect on electricity prices or safety would come later, as specific projects move forward.

stories.title: Brewers erase four-run deficit to beat Rays 5-4, take 2-0 World Series lead
stories.summary: Sal Frelick tied it with a home run and Cooper Pratt hit the go-ahead single in the seventh.

article.background: The World Series is baseball's championship, played between the winners of the American League and National League. This year the Milwaukee Brewers face the Tampa Bay Rays. Norm covered Game 1 on Friday, when Milwaukee won 3-2. Tampa Bay won the American League Championship Series in six games over Cleveland, its third trip to the World Series in the franchise's 29 seasons.
article.what_happened: Milwaukee trailed 4-0 but came back to win Game 2 by a score of 5-4 on Saturday night. Sal Frelick tied the score with his first home run in three months. Cooper Pratt then hit a go-ahead single in the seventh inning. Tampa Bay made one error and two other plays that could have been called errors. A runner was also thrown out at the plate. The win gives Milwaukee a 2-0 lead in the series. It was the second time this postseason the Brewers erased a four-run deficit.
article.why_it_matters: For fans, this series is a chance to watch a team come from behind in the most important games of the year. A 2-0 lead means Milwaukee needs only two more wins in the next five games to take the title. The series decides which team gets the trophy for the year.

stories.title: Kimi Antonelli takes pole for US Grand Prix on weekend he could clinch first world title
stories.summary: The Mercedes driver beat Max Verstappen by 0.179 seconds at the Circuit of the Americas.

article.background: Formula 1 is the top level of car racing, with teams and drivers competing across a season of races. Kimi Antonelli is a 20-year-old Italian driver for Mercedes. He has a 102-point lead over his Mercedes team-mate George Russell in the drivers' championship. The title goes to the driver with the most points at the end of the season. Antonelli is the Mercedes driver who can win it this weekend.
article.what_happened: Antonelli took pole position for the United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas. Pole position means starting first on the grid. He beat Red Bull's Max Verstappen by 0.179 seconds. Red Bull's Isack Hadjar finished third in qualifying, ahead of Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton. Russell was sixth. This was Antonelli's first pole since the Belgian Grand Prix in July.
article.why_it_matters: If Antonelli wins Sunday's race, he becomes world champion, and at 20 he would be the youngest ever to hold the title. For most fans, the result shows how close the season has become. The title race is decided by points across the whole season, so a single race can change who leads.

quote.text: It feels good to be back.
